title: AXI3 Interleaving vs AXI4 Write Order
description: Both examples assume write addresses A then B were accepted; inspect the W-channel beats to see how AXI3 WID could identify interleaved data while AXI4 must finish A before B.
labels: AXI3: WID identifies each write-data beat
AXI4 write data follows address order

phases.name: A0 · WID 0
phases.description: First beat of transaction A. AXI3 carries WID so the destination can associate this beat with AWID 0.

phases.name: B0 · WID 1
phases.description: A beat from transaction B is interleaved before A finishes. AXI3 permits this only within its write-data interleaving rules and declared capability.

phases.name: A1 · WLAST
phases.description: Transaction A finishes; WID still identifies its write-data stream.

phases.name: B1 · WLAST
phases.description: Transaction B finishes after the interleaved A beat.

phases.name: A0
phases.description: AXI4 has no WID. The first data beat belongs to the first accepted write address, transaction A.

phases.name: A1 · WLAST
phases.description: All data for A completes before any data for B is forwarded.

phases.name: B0
phases.description: Only after A finishes can the W channel begin transaction B.

phases.name: B1 · WLAST
phases.description: The W stream remains attributable through accepted address order rather than a per-beat WID.

annotations.message: Interleaving is an AXI3 capability, not permission to mix beats without WID and the required component support.
AXI4 removes WID and requires a master—and a combining interconnect—to issue write data in write-address order.
